)

data_dir <- "data"
have_data <- file.exists(file.path(data_dir, "person.parquet"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_data || nzchar(Sys.getenv("MOSPI_KEY")))

```{r no-key, eval = !knitr::opts_chunk$get("eval"), echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(

```

This article shows how education expenditure in India changes with state,
district, location, gender, class, and private coaching. The data is the NSS
80th round Comprehensive Modular Survey on Education (CMS-E, 2025).

All the values are weighted means of annual expenditure per student, in
rupees (Rs). The population is students who are currently enrolled in school.
Total expenditure is school expenditure plus private coaching expenditure.

## Get the data

You must have an API key for the
[MoSPI Microdata Portal](https://microdata.gov.in). Set the environment
variable `MOSPI_KEY` in `~/.Renviron`. The download is approximately 8.5 MB.

```{r setup}
library(educationsurveyindia)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

if (!file.exists(file.path(data_dir, "person.parquet"))) {
  esi_build(output_dir = data_dir)
}
con <- esi_connect(data_dir)
```

This article removes a value if the group has less than `MIN_N` students.
Cells of a heatmap use the smaller `MIN_N_CELL`.

```{r helpers}
MIN_N <- 30
MIN_N_CELL <- 15
rs <- label_dollar(prefix = "Rs ", big.mark = ",", accuracy = 1)
blue <- "#2a78d6"
orange <- "#eb6834"

# Replace codes with labels, for example sector "1" with "rural"
decode <- function(d, col) {
  d[[col]] <- esi_decode(con, "person", col, d[[col]])
  d
}

# Ratio of the mean of group `num` to the mean of group `den` in column `col`
gap <- function(d, col, num, den, keys, min_n = MIN_N) {
  m <- merge(d[d[[col]] == num, ], d[d[[col]] == den, ], by = keys)
  m$ratio <- m$mean_total_expenditure.x / m$mean_total_expenditure.y
  m$ratio[pmin(m$n_students.x, m$n_students.y) < min_n] <- NA
  m[c(keys, "ratio")]
}

# Limits of a log scale that put a ratio of 1 at the center of the palette
symmetric <- function(l) 2^(c(-1, 1) * max(abs(log2(l)), na.rm = TRUE))

state_map <- function(state_name, value, name, labels = waiver(), ...) {
  ggplot(esi_attach_geometry(data.frame(state = state_name, value = value))) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = value), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", labels = labels, name = name, na.value = "grey85", ...) +
    theme_void()
}

# School classes only: the diploma courses have too few students for a heatmap
school_class <- function(code) {
  cl <- esi_class_label(code)
  factor(cl, levels = grep("Diploma", levels(cl), value = TRUE, invert = TRUE))
}

# Rows with no value are removed
heatmap <- function(d, x, y, fill) {
  d <- d[d[[y]] %in% d[[y]][!is.na(d[[fill]])], ]
  ggplot(d, aes(.data[[x]], .data[[y]], fill = .data[[fill]])) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
}
```

## National mean

```{r national}
national <- esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = NULL)
national
```

Do not calculate the national mean from the state means and the record
counts. The record counts are not survey weights.

## By state

`ESI_STATE_CODES` gives the state name for each NSS state code.

```{r by-state}
by_state <- esi_expenditure_by_state(con)
by_state$state_name <- ESI_STATE_CODES[by_state$state]
by_state <- by_state[by_state$n_students >= MIN_N, ]
```

The error bars are an approximate 95% interval. The standard error is the
weighted standard deviation divided by the square root of the number of
students. It is not a design-based standard error, because it does not use
the strata and the first-stage units of the survey.

```{r by-state-se}
se <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  WITH x AS (
    SELECT state, weight,
      COALESCE(school_exp_total, 0) + COALESCE(private_coaching_exp_total, 0) AS total
    FROM person WHERE currently_enrolled_school = '1'
  ), m AS (
    SELECT state, SUM(total * weight) / SUM(weight) AS mean, COUNT(*) AS n FROM x GROUP BY state
  )
  SELECT state, SQRT(SUM(weight * POWER(total - mean, 2)) / SUM(weight) / ANY_VALUE(n)) AS se
  FROM x JOIN m USING (state)
  GROUP BY state
")
by_state$se <- se$se[match(by_state$state, se$state)]
```

```{r by-state-plot, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(by_state, aes(mean_total_expenditure, reorder(state_name, mean_total_expenditure))) +
  geom_col(fill = blue) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(
    xmin = pmax(0, mean_total_expenditure - 1.96 * se),
    xmax = mean_total_expenditure + 1.96 * se
  ), orientation = "y", width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = national$mean_total_expenditure, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = rs, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean expenditure (Rs/year)", y = NULL,
    title = "Education expenditure by state",
    subtitle = "Dashed line: national mean. Error bars: approximate 95% interval"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

`esi_attach_geometry()` adds the state boundaries for a map. It downloads
the boundaries from bharatviz.org.

```{r by-state-map, fig.height = 7}
state_map(by_state$state_name, by_state$mean_total_expenditure, "Rs/year", rs, transform = "log10") +
  labs(title = "Mean education expenditure", subtitle = "Grey: no data or less than MIN_N students")
```

The highest and the lowest states:

```{r state-extremes}
ext <- by_state[c(which.max(by_state$mean_total_expenditure), which.min(by_state$mean_total_expenditure)), ]
ext[, c("state_name", "n_students", "mean_total_expenditure")]
```

## By location and gender

`esi_decode()` changes the codes of `sector` and `gender` to labels.

```{r location-gender}
by_sector <- decode(esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = "sector"), "sector")
by_sector[, c("sector", "n_students", "mean_total_expenditure")]

by_gender <- decode(esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = "gender"), "gender")
by_gender[, c("gender", "n_students", "mean_total_expenditure")]
```

### Location and gender by state

The maps show the urban mean divided by the rural mean, and the male mean
divided by the female mean, for each state. A value of 1 is no difference.
A ratio is removed if one of the two groups has less than `MIN_N` students.

```{r gap-by-state}
sector_state <- decode(esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = c("state", "sector")), "sector")
urban_rural <- gap(sector_state, "sector", "urban", "rural", "state")

gender_state <- decode(esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = c("state", "gender")), "gender")
male_female <- gap(gender_state, "gender", "male", "female", "state")
```

```{r gap-maps, fig.height = 7}
state_map(ESI_STATE_CODES[urban_rural$state], urban_rural$ratio, "Urban / rural",
  transform = "log2", limits = symmetric, breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)
) +
  labs(title = "Urban expenditure relative to rural expenditure")

state_map(ESI_STATE_CODES[male_female$state], male_female$ratio, "Male / female",
  transform = "log2", limits = symmetric, breaks = c(0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2)
) +
  labs(title = "Male expenditure relative to female expenditure")
```

## By district

The `district` column is a serial number in each state. The data does not
give the district names. Thus the district figures have no names and no map.
Each point is one district.

```{r by-district}
by_district <- esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = c("state", "district"))
by_district <- by_district[by_district$n_students >= MIN_N, ]
by_district$rank <- rank(by_district$mean_total_expenditure, ties.method = "first")

ggplot(by_district, aes(rank, mean_total_expenditure)) +
  geom_point(color = blue, size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = national$mean_total_expenditure, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = rs, transform = "log10") +
  labs(x = "District, in order of expenditure", y = "Mean expenditure (Rs/year)",
    title = "Education expenditure by district",
    subtitle = sprintf("%d districts with %d or more students. Dashed line: national mean", nrow(by_district), MIN_N)
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## By class

`esi_class_label()` puts the `enrolment_level` codes in school order. The raw
code for pre-primary is `"15"`. Thus, without this function, pre-primary is last.

```{r by-class}
by_class <- esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = "enrolment_level")
by_class$class <- esi_class_label(by_class$enrolment_level)
by_class <- by_class[!is.na(by_class$class), ]

parts <- rbind(
  data.frame(class = by_class$class, type = "School", value = by_class$mean_school_expenditure),
  data.frame(class = by_class$class, type = "Private coaching", value = by_class$mean_coaching_expenditure)
)
parts$type <- factor(parts$type, levels = c("Private coaching", "School"))

ggplot(parts, aes(class, value, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(School = blue, `Private coaching` = orange), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = rs, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean expenditure (Rs/year)", title = "Education expenditure increases with class") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "top")
```

### Gender gap by class and location

The plot shows the female mean divided by the male mean for each class. A
value of 1 is no difference.

```{r gender-gap-class}
gc <- esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = c("sector", "enrolment_level", "gender"))
gc <- decode(decode(gc, "sector"), "gender")
gc_all <- decode(esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = c("enrolment_level", "gender")), "gender")
gc_all$sector <- "all"

fm <- gap(rbind(gc, gc_all[names(gc)]), "gender", "female", "male", c("sector", "enrolment_level"))
fm$class <- school_class(fm$enrolment_level)
fm <- fm[!is.na(fm$class), ]

ggplot(fm, aes(class, ratio, color = sector, group = sector)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(all = "black", rural = "#1baf7a", urban = "#4a3aa7"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Female / male", title = "Female expenditure relative to male expenditure") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "top")
```

### State and class

The first heatmap shows the mean expenditure. The second heatmap shows the
expenditure of each class relative to the mean of the state. A value of 2 is
two times the state mean. Grey cells have less than `MIN_N_CELL` students. The
rows are in order of the state mean.

```{r state-class}
state_order <- by_state$state_name[order(by_state$mean_total_expenditure)]

sc <- esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = c("state", "enrolment_level"))
sc$class <- school_class(sc$enrolment_level)
sc <- sc[!is.na(sc$class) & sc$state %in% by_state$state, ]
sc$mean_total_expenditure[sc$n_students < MIN_N_CELL] <- NA
state_mean <- by_state$mean_total_expenditure[match(sc$state, by_state$state)]
sc$relative <- sc$mean_total_expenditure / state_mean
sc$state_name <- factor(ESI_STATE_CODES[sc$state], levels = state_order)
```

```{r state-class-plot, fig.height = 9}
heatmap(sc, "class", "state_name", "mean_total_expenditure") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", transform = "log10", labels = rs,
    na.value = "grey85", name = "Rs/year"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Expenditure by state and class")

heatmap(sc, "class", "state_name", "relative") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", transform = "log2", limits = symmetric,
    na.value = "grey85", breaks = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4), labels = c("0.25", "0.5", "1", "2", "4"),
    name = "Relative to\nstate mean"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Expenditure by class, relative to the state mean")
```

The next heatmaps divide each state and class into rural and urban, and into
male and female. The cells are smaller, so there are more grey cells.

```{r state-class-split, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 9}
split_heatmap <- function(col, keep) {
  d <- decode(esi_expenditure_by_state(con, by = c("state", col, "enrolment_level")), col)
  d$class <- school_class(d$enrolment_level)
  d <- d[!is.na(d$class) & d$state %in% by_state$state & d[[col]] %in% keep, ]
  d$mean_total_expenditure[d$n_students < MIN_N_CELL] <- NA
  d[[col]] <- factor(d[[col]], levels = keep)
  d$state_name <- factor(ESI_STATE_CODES[d$state], levels = state_order)
  heatmap(d, "class", "state_name", "mean_total_expenditure") +
    facet_wrap(col) +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", transform = "log10", labels = rs,
      na.value = "grey85", name = "Rs/year"
    )
}

split_heatmap("sector", c("rural", "urban")) + labs(title = "Expenditure by state, class, and location")
split_heatmap("gender", c("male", "female")) + labs(title = "Expenditure by state, class, and gender")
```

## Expenditure categories

`esi_expenditure_by_category()` gives the mean of each expenditure line item.

```{r categories}
category_labels <- c(
  school_exp_course_fee = "School: course fee",
  school_exp_transport = "School: transport",
  school_exp_uniform = "School: uniform",
  school_exp_textbooks_stationery = "School: textbooks and stationery",
  school_exp_other = "School: other",
  private_coaching_exp_course_fee = "Coaching: course fee",
  private_coaching_exp_transport = "Coaching: transport",
  private_coaching_exp_uniform = "Coaching: uniform",
  private_coaching_exp_textbooks_material = "Coaching: textbooks and material",
  private_coaching_exp_other = "Coaching: other",
  hostel_fee_expenditure = "Hostel fee"
)

cats <- esi_expenditure_by_category(con)
cats <- cats[order(-cats$mean_expenditure), ]
cats$label <- category_labels[cats$category]
knitr::kable(cats[c("label", "mean_expenditure")],
  digits = 0, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  col.names = c("Category", "Mean annual expenditure (Rs)")
)
```

### Categories by class

The rows are in order of the national mean. The color scale is logarithmic.
Grey cells have no expenditure.

```{r category-class}
category_heatmap <- function(by = NULL, keep = NULL) {
  d <- esi_expenditure_by_category(con, by = c("enrolment_level", by))
  d$class <- school_class(d$enrolment_level)
  d <- d[!is.na(d$class), ]
  d$mean_expenditure[d$mean_expenditure == 0] <- NA
  d$label <- factor(category_labels[d$category], levels = rev(cats$label))
  if (!is.null(by)) {
    d <- decode(d, by)
    d <- d[d[[by]] %in% keep, ]
    d[[by]] <- factor(d[[by]], levels = keep)
  }
  p <- heatmap(d, "class", "label", "mean_expenditure") +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", transform = "log10", labels = rs, breaks = 10^(0:4),
      na.value = "grey85", name = "Rs/year"
    )
  if (!is.null(by)) p <- p + facet_wrap(by)
  p
}

category_heatmap() + labs(title = "Expenditure by category and class")
```

```{r category-class-split, fig.width = 10}
category_heatmap("sector", c("rural", "urban")) + labs(title = "Expenditure by category, class, and location")
category_heatmap("gender", c("male", "female")) + labs(title = "Expenditure by category, class, and gender")
```

## Private coaching

`esi_coaching()` gives the share of students with private coaching, and the
mean coaching expenditure of these students.

```{r coaching}
coaching <- esi_coaching(con, by = NULL)
coaching

decode(esi_coaching(con, by = "sector"), "sector")
decode(esi_coaching(con, by = "gender"), "gender")
```

CMS-E does not record why a student gets coaching.
Thus the data cannot show if the coaching is for entrance examinations.

```{r coaching-class}
cc <- esi_coaching(con, by = "enrolment_level")
cc$class <- esi_class_label(cc$enrolment_level)
cc <- cc[!is.na(cc$class), ]

ggplot(cc, aes(class, coaching_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = blue, width = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Students with private coaching", title = "Private coaching increases with class") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r coaching-class-table}
knitr::kable(cc[order(cc$class), c("class", "n_students", "coaching_rate", "mean_coaching_expenditure_coached")],
  digits = c(0, 0, 3, 0), row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  col.names = c("Class", "Students", "Coaching rate", "Mean expenditure if coached (Rs)")
)
```

### Coaching by state

```{r coaching-state, fig.height = 8}
cs <- esi_coaching(con)
cs$state_name <- ESI_STATE_CODES[cs$state]
cs <- cs[cs$n_students >= MIN_N, ]

ggplot(cs, aes(coaching_rate, reorder(state_name, coaching_rate))) +
  geom_col(fill = blue) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Students with private coaching", y = NULL, title = "Private coaching by state") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r coaching-map, fig.height = 7}
state_map(cs$state_name, cs$coaching_rate, "Coached", label_percent()) +
  labs(title = "Students with private coaching")
```

The heatmap shows the coaching rate for each state and class. The rows are
in order of the state coaching rate. Grey cells have less than `MIN_N_CELL`
students.

```{r coaching-state-class, fig.height = 9}
csc <- esi_coaching(con, by = c("state", "enrolment_level"))
csc$class <- school_class(csc$enrolment_level)
csc <- csc[!is.na(csc$class) & csc$state %in% cs$state, ]
csc$coaching_rate[csc$n_students < MIN_N_CELL] <- NA
csc$state_name <- factor(ESI_STATE_CODES[csc$state], levels = cs$state_name[order(cs$coaching_rate)])

heatmap(csc, "class", "state_name", "coaching_rate") +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", labels = label_percent(), na.value = "grey85", name = "Coached") +
  labs(title = "Private coaching by state and class")
```

### Coaching by district

```{r coaching-district}
cd <- esi_coaching(con, by = c("state", "district"))
cd <- cd[cd$n_students >= MIN_N, ]
cd$rank <- rank(cd$coaching_rate, ties.method = "first")

ggplot(cd, aes(rank, coaching_rate)) +
  geom_point(color = blue, size = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "District, in order of coaching rate", y = "Students with private coaching",
    title = "Private coaching by district",
    subtitle = sprintf("%d districts with %d or more students", nrow(cd), MIN_N)
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r disconnect}
esi_disconnect(con)
```
